label: OBIB case 2 (derive-first): LBTC Transfer, deployment-22,500,000, balances derived not fetched
record_definition: distinct accounts touched by a Transfer in blocks 22,400,000-22,500,000, excluding 0x0
method: derive-first: balances summed from the token's full Transfer history; ZERO eth_call round trips

correctness.account_count: 7,634 exact. With 0x0 included it is 7,635; 0x0 is the mint/burn counterparty, not a holder (975 such legs in the window), and OBIB excludes it too.
correctness.balances_vs_balanceOf: 39/39 sampled accounts matched balanceOf() at block 22,500,000 - the 10 largest, 10 smallest non-zero, 10 zero-balance and 10 by address order. All 13 zero-balance accounts matched, which is the hard case (received, then fully sent out).
correctness.verified_against: eth_call balanceOf(address) at pinned block 22,500,000 on an archive endpoint

not_apples_to_apples: Deliberately different method, identical result. OBIB windows to 100,001 blocks and makes one balanceOf() per account; this indexes 2,611,334 blocks (the token's whole life) and makes none. We do strictly more block coverage and strictly fewer RPC round trips, and the output is verified equal. A window-only run cannot produce absolute balances at all - which is precisely why the benchmark needs the RPC augmentation and we do not.

obib_window_only.note: OBIB's own block range, for the closest comparison on *range*: 22,400,000-22,500,000. Fast, but it cannot produce the case's output - absolute balances need history before the window, which is exactly why the benchmark makes balanceOf() calls. Published so the 49.18s headline is not mistaken for a like-for-like range.

reproduce: git checkout the obib-case2/ nest, then: nuthatch bench backfill --dir . --from 19888667 --to 22500000 --runs 3 --seal-direct --concurrency 8 --rpc "$RPC". Verified from a clean `git archive` checkout with no local state.
